land.text: the Qara Qoyunlu homeland north of Lake Van and near Mosul; the page makes them Jalayirid vassals from about 1375, not conquerors of Jalayirid land

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessors: Jalayirids, Sutayids, Timurids. No land was taken from the Jalayirids at the birth; the tribe already held the Van and Mosul pastures.

land.text: Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu 'took Iraq, Azerbaijan and western Iran' by 1468

capitals.name: Erciş (Erdjish), summer pastures
capitals.note: Infobox lists Erciş (summer pastures), Mosul (winter pastures) and Tabriz without years; Qara Yusuf was buried at Erciş (Qara Yusuf page). The span 1374-1410 is my reading.

capitals.name: Tabriz
capitals.note: Qara Yusuf page: Tabriz 'his capital'; Qara Yusuf enters Tabriz in fall 1409 and defeats Ahmad Jalayir near it on 30 August 1410. Jahan Shah set out from Tabriz in 1466 (Jahan Shah page).

correction.text: lands north of Lake Van and near Mosul

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the founding year, one year before Cliopatria's first shape (1375). The page: the ruling family 'held lands north of Lake Van and near Mosul' by the 14th century; Bayram Khwaja first ruler 1374-1378.

correction.text: eastern Turkey (Van, Mush, Bitlis, Diyarbakir) and northern Iraq (Mosul); the Azerbaijan plateau around Tabriz was Jalayirid

keyframe_review.note: 338,766 km2 with Tabriz, all Iranian Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan and Armenia is too much: the page makes the Qara Qoyunlu Jalayirid vassals from about 1375 with a core north of Lake Van and near Mosul (Shaykh Uways beat them at Mush in 1366), and the Jalayirid page has Tabriz the Jalayirid capital 1358-1388. Correction removes Iran, Azerbaijan and Armenia (about 163,000 km2 remain: eastern Turkey and northern Iraq). The 1384 Mardin submission is already inside.

correction.text: eastern Turkey and northern Iraq without Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan and Armenia

keyframe_review.note: Same fault as 1375 (294,134 km2 including Iranian Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan and Armenia); the page's only dated gain in this span is Mardin in 1384.

151,717 km2: eastern Anatolia, Mardin, Diyarbakir and northern Iraq, consistent with the page's 1384 Mardin submission. The page says Timur defeated the Qara Qoyunlu in 1400 (year only), so the last shape year (1401) is one or two years late; the 1400 loss event ends it.

correction.text: Qara Yusuf's base in eastern Anatolia after his return in 1405-06: the shape plus the Van region whose Timurid governor he forced to submit

keyframe_review.note: 20,290 km2 around Erzurum and Bayburt is too small and in the wrong place for 1407-1409: the page has Qara Yusuf back in Anatolia after Timur's death (1405), forcing 'Timur's Van governor' to submit (undated), winning at Nakhchivan on 14 October 1406 and Sardrud on 20 April 1408, and taking Mardin in 1409 (Qara Yusuf page). Correction adds Van province; the holdings 1410-1414 are the new keyframe qara-qoyunlu_1410.

correction.text: Azerbaijan, Armenia and Iraq as in Cliopatria's 1415 shape, held from 1410

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: by 1410 the Qara Qoyunlu hold Tabriz and Azerbaijan (Ahmad Jalayir killed near Tabriz, 30 August 1410), Baghdad and Iraq ('Baghdad captured', 1410), Armenia ('came under Qara Qoyunlu control', 1410) and Mardin (1409); Cliopatria's 1415 shape shows exactly that, four years early. [fx-15 review] Zanjan and Soltaniyeh stay in this shape: the Qara Qoyunlu page puts the Timurid capture of Sultaniya and Qazvin 'at the same time' as Jahan Shah becoming independent after Shah Rukh's death in 1447 (so they were not Timurid just before 1447), and the Jahan Shah page has the same order; the fx-15 subtraction (Timurid 1410-1446) was reverted.

440,263 km2: Azerbaijan, Armenia, northern and central Iraq, Soltaniyeh (governorship given to Jahan Shah in 1415) and eastern Anatolia. It omits lower Iraq (Hillah, Wasit, Basra), which the Jalayirid page keeps in Jalayirid hands until 1431-32. Timurid occupation of Tabriz in 1421 is a passing episode shown by the contest events. Reviewer (me-09-h): from 1432 the keyframe qara-qoyunlu_1432 adds lower Iraq. correction.text: Cliopatria's 1440 shape plus Hamadan, Qazvin, Qom, Markazi (Saveh), Esfahan, Yazd and Fars (Shiraz)

Provinces named from cities (my reading), about 955,000 km2 by cell count, nearly twice the infobox's 520,000 km2, so the infobox map omits central Iran.

The Uzun Hasan page lists Harput (1465) under his Dulkadir war, so the Qara Qoyunlu east frontier stands.

region.text: the lands north of Lake Van and near Mosul

ledger.note: 1374: Bayram Khwaja founds the Qara Qoyunlu confederation north of Lake Van and near Mosul. Infobox 'Established: 1374', first ruler Bayram Khwaja 1374-1378; Britannica (cited on the page) gives 'about 1375', which is Cliopatria's start.
1384: Qara Muhammad invades Mardin and receives the submission of its Artuqid ruler ('Invaded Mardin in 1384 and received the submission of its Artuqid ruler').

region.text: the Qara Qoyunlu lands of Cliopatria's 1395-1401 shape

ledger.note: 1400: Timur defeats the Qara Qoyunlu and Qara Yusuf flees to the Mamluks. The page: 'Timur defeated the Qara Qoyunlu' (1400, year only, no land named). Timur then has a governor at Van (Qara Yusuf later 'forced Timur's Van governor to submit'). Cliopatria's row has no shape for 1402-1406; the dynasty survives in exile in Damascus until Timur's death in 1405.

region.text: the Van region under Timur's governor

ledger.note: Page silent on the year: after Timur's death in 1405 Qara Yusuf returned to Anatolia and 'forced Timur's Van governor to submit' (Qara Qoyunlu page, no year); bridged at 1406, the year of his victory at Nakhchivan.
14 October 1406: Qara Yusuf defeats the Timurid Abu Bakr at the Battle of Nakhchivan and reoccupies Tabriz.
20 April 1408: Qara Yusuf's victory at Sardrud, where Miran Shah is killed, ends Timurid power in Azerbaijan.

20 April 1408: Qara Yusuf's victory at Sardrud, where Miran Shah is killed ('Qara Yusuf inflicted a decisive defeat on them at the Battle of Sardrud'), settles the contest for Tabriz that began when he 'recovered Tabriz after defeating Abu Bakr' in 1406. The contest_end above moved no land, so the Timurids still held the Tabriz district when the 1410 keyframe claimed it (conflict_places, 119 cells East Azarbaijan); the gain closes the gap (fx-15, F157). Mirror in timurid-empire.
1409: the Artuqid state of Mardin is ended ('Mardin Artuqids ended', Qara Yusuf page; the Qara Qoyunlu page: 'Mardin taken', 1409).
1409: Qara Yusuf ends the Artuqid dynasty of Mardin, vassal since 1384.

1409: Qara Yusuf sends a force to Sultaniyya and Qazvin (page: 'force sent to Sultaniyya and Qazvin'); Jahan Shah receives the governorship of Soltaniyeh in 1415. Holder before: Timurid Azerbaijan (my reading). Reviewer (me-09-h, 2026-10-25): the Qara Yusuf page says only that 'Another invasion force was sent to capture Sultaniyya and Qazvin under the command of Rustam Beg' and gives no outcome, so confidence 1. [fx-15 review: restored after fx-15 deleted it; the deletion read the Timurid capture of Sultaniya and Qazvin as undated, but the Qara Qoyunlu page places it in 1447, after which Jahan Shah 'managed to capture the cities of Sultaniya, Hamadan and Qazvin'.]

Fall 1409: Qara Yusuf enters Tabriz (Qara Qoyunlu page: 'Qara Yusuf entered Tabriz'); Ahmad Jalayir, whom he kills the next year, is the contesting ruler; the failed raid on Shirvan and Shaki is the same autumn.

region.text: Baghdad and the Iraq of its province

ledger.note: 1410: Baghdad captured ('Baghdad captured', 1410, year only); the Qara Yusuf page has Iraq passing to him. Lower Iraq stays Jalayirid until 1432.
1410: 'Armenia came under Qara Qoyunlu control' (year only). The previous holder is not named by the page.
1410: the seat moves to Tabriz, 'his capital' in the Qara Yusuf page, after the victory over Ahmad Jalayir; the infobox lists Erciş, Mosul and Tabriz without years.
30 August 1410: the battle near Tabriz in which Ahmad Jalayir is defeated and executed.
30 August 1410: Qara Yusuf takes Tabriz and Azerbaijan from the Jalayirid Ahmad, whom he defeats near Tabriz and executes; Azerbaijan was his share under the agreement with Ahmad.

1420-21: Shah Rukh defeats Qara Iskander and the Timurids briefly occupy Tabriz in 1421 ('Shah Rukh defeated Qara Iskander; Timurids briefly occupied Tabriz in 1421'). Qara Yusuf died on 17 November 1420 on the way to battle (Qara Yusuf page).
October 1431: the Qara Qoyunlu prince Aspan captures al-Hilla, the Jalayirid remnant's seat (the page: 'captured al-Hella' 'in October 1431').

region.text: lower Iraq: Hillah, Wasit and Basra

ledger.note: 1432: the Jalayirid dynasty is 'finally eliminated by the Qara Qoyunlu' (the last ruler Hosayn II was killed on 9 November 1431).

region.text: lower Iraq: Hillah, Wasit and Basra

ledger.note: 1432: lower Iraq (Hillah, with Wasit and Basra, the Jalayirid capital 1411-1432) passes to the Qara Qoyunlu. Cliopatria's 1440 shape includes it.

1434-35: Shah Rukh's third Azerbaijan expedition succeeds and Jahan Shah becomes his vassal ('Timurids succeeded in a third expedition. Jahan Shah became their vassal'); the Timurids draw the vassal tint, this state's dossier records only the end of the fighting.

ledger.counterpart: Ispend's line at Baghdad (Qara Qoyunlu appanage)
ledger.note: 9 June 1446: Jahan Shah captures Baghdad after a seven-month siege ('After a siege of seven months, Baghdad was captured on 9 June 1446'). The page names the previous holder: his brother Ispend 'had ruled over Baghdad and its environs for twelve years' until his death in 1445, an appanage outside Jahan Shah's control; Cliopatria's shapes show Baghdad inside since 1410.
1447: after Shah Rukh's death 'Sultaniyya, Hamadan and Qazvin were taken' (Jahan Shah independent).

region.text: Saveh, Qum, Isfahan, Shiraz and Yazd

ledger.note: 1452-53: 'After the death of the Timurid governor of Fars, Jahan Shah takes Saveh, Qum, Isfahan, Shiraz, and Yazd.' The provinces are my reading of the cities; 1453 is placed to match Cliopatria's shape breaks (page: 1452-1453).
Summer 1458: Jahan Shah occupies Herat ('Occupied Herat for six months'; the Qara Qoyunlu page: 'for a few months').
1458: Jahan Shah turns back from Herat 'due to a revolt by his son Hasan Ali and Abu Said's march on Tabriz'.

Page silent on the year: the page says Jahan Shah extended Qara Qoyunlu territory 'to its largest extent', including 'central Iran, and eventually Kerman' (the Qara Qoyunlu page has Qasim Beg assigned to Kerman, undated). Placed beside the Isfahan-Shiraz-Yazd conquest. [fx-15: moved from 1453 to 1463 to agree with the keyframes, which add Kerman only in qara-qoyunlu_1463 (1453-1462 leave it out); the Jahan Shah page puts Kerman after the 1452-53 conquests ('even eventually Kerman') and 'Qasim Beg was assigned to Kerman' after the 1458 events, both undated. Mirror loss in timurid-empire.]

1464: Pir Budaq, 'who had rebelled while controlling Baghdad', is defeated and executed by Mirza Muhammad; Baghdad returns to Jahan Shah (the Qara Qoyunlu page: 'Baghdad rulers expelled'). Start of the revolt not given.

region.text: the sanjak of Capakcur near Bingol and Mush

ledger.note: 30 October (or 11 November) 1467: Jahan Shah, who had set out from Tabriz on 16 May 1466 and withdrawn for the winter from Mush, is defeated and killed at the Battle of Chapakchur by Uzun Hasan. The zone is the Chapakchur (Bingol) frontier.
1468: the fighting ends with Aq Qoyunlu victory and Hasan Ali's brief reign (1467-68).
1468: 'Aq Qoyunlu defeated the Qara Qoyunlu and took Iraq, Azerbaijan and western Iran' (the page's own phrase, year only).
1468: the Qara Qoyunlu state ends after Jahan Shah's death at Chapakchur; infobox 'Disestablished: 1468', last ruler Hasan Ali 1467-1468, successor Aq Qoyunlu.

wars.name: Timur's campaign against the Qara Qoyunlu and Jalayirids
wars.outcome: The Timurids defeat both in 1400; Qara Yusuf flees to the Mamluks in Damascus, is handed over to Timur and released in 1405 after Timur's death.
wars.note: Years only; the Qara Yusuf page gives 1402 for the return to Mesopotamia and 1403 for the defeat at the Algami Canal near Baghdad.

wars.name: Qara Yusuf's reconquest of Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: Qara Yusuf wins at Nakhchivan (14 October 1406) and Sardrud (20 April 1408), where Miran Shah is killed; Tabriz is his.

wars.name: Qara Qoyunlu-Jalayirid war for Tabriz and Iraq
wars.outcome: Qara Yusuf enters Tabriz in fall 1409 and kills Ahmad Jalayir near it on 30 August 1410; Baghdad and Iraq pass to him.

wars.name: Timurid campaigns against Qara Iskander
wars.outcome: Shah Rukh defeats Qara Iskander in 1420-21 (Tabriz briefly occupied in 1421) and 1429; the third expedition of 1434-35 succeeds and Jahan Shah becomes a Timurid vassal until 1447.

wars.name: Qara Qoyunlu conquest of the last Jalayirids in lower Iraq

zones.text: lower Iraq: Hillah, Wasit and Basra

wars.outcome: Aspan takes al-Hilla in October 1431; Hosayn II is killed on 9 November 1431 and the Jalayirids are eliminated in 1432.

wars.name: Jahan Shah's conquest of western and central Iran
wars.outcome: Baghdad (9 June 1446), Sultaniyya, Hamadan and Qazvin (1447) and Saveh, Qum, Isfahan, Shiraz and Yazd (1452-53) pass to the Qara Qoyunlu.

wars.name: Jahan Shah's Herat expedition
wars.outcome: Herat occupied for a few months (six, on the Jahan Shah page) in summer 1458, then abandoned after Hasan Ali's revolt and Abu Said's march on Tabriz.

wars.name: Revolt of Pir Budaq at Baghdad
wars.outcome: Pir Budaq, governor of Baghdad, rebelled; he was defeated and executed in 1464 by Mirza Muhammad.
wars.note: Start year of the revolt not given by the pages.

wars.name: Qara Qoyunlu-Aq Qoyunlu war
wars.outcome: Jahan Shah's 1466 attempt on Diyarbakir fails; he is defeated and killed at Chapakchur in October/November 1467; Uzun Hasan takes Iraq, Azerbaijan and western Iran by 1468 and the state ends.

certainty.note: A tribal confederation with summer and winter pastures; no treaty or survey frontier in the pages. Rule 9: every border is approximate. The peace with Shah Rukh (1436) fixed no line.

notes:
Six pages cited (state article, Qara Yusuf, Jahan Shah, Jalayirid Sultanate, Aq Qoyunlu, Uzun Hasan); the last three are shared with the Aq Qoyunlu and Hashemite Arab Federation dossiers of this batch. Page budget: up to 5; the Uzun Hasan page was opened for the Aq Qoyunlu dossier and used here only for Chapakchur.
Cliopatria row problems: (1) the 1375 and 1385 shapes (338,766 and 294,134 km2) cover Iranian Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan and Armenia, where the Jalayirids ruled from Tabriz; the page makes the Qara Qoyunlu Jalayirid vassals from about 1375 with a core north of Lake Van and near Mosul. (2) 1402-1406 has no shape: Timur's 1400 victory and Qara Yusuf's exile are recorded as a loss event and the dynasty continues. (3) The 1440 and 1463 shapes match the infobox area (520,000 km2) but omit Hamadan, Qazvin and central Iran (Isfahan, Shiraz, Yazd, Kerman), which the Jahan Shah and Qara Qoyunlu pages put inside from 1447/1452-53; with them the realm is about 955,000 km2 (cell count x 253 km2). (4) Cliopatria's vassalage row 1407-1467 (rel-vassalage-of-qara-qoyunlu-to-timurid-empire) is too long: the pages make Jahan Shah a Timurid vassal only from 1434-35 to Shah Rukh's death in 1447 (the Timurid dossier agrees). (5) Cliopatria ends 1467; the infobox says 1468 and the dossier follows the infobox.
Vassal relations of this state are recorded as the overlord's events: Jalayirid suzerainty from about 1375 (page: 'vassals of the Jalayirids', year only), Timurid 1434/35-1447; Qara Yusuf's refuge with the Mamluks was asylum, not vassalage. The reviewer should not expect vassal_start events with this state as the vassal.
Not settled: the dates of Qara Muhammad's reign (the page gives only the first and last rulers; no ruler strip written), the date of Kerman's conquest (confidence 1), the start of Pir Budaq's revolt, the holder of Baghdad before June 1446, the Qara Qoyunlu-Mamluk border (Qara Yusuf raided Aintab, undated), Erzincan under Abu Said and Bitlis by marriage (named, undated, not drawn). The Qara Qoyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu pages do not mention each other's borders in eastern Anatolia before 1465-67.
Counterparts needing dossiers: Artuqids of Mardin (1384 vassal, ended 1409); Pir Budaq's Baghdad (a short-lived rebel holding, probably not worth a dossier). The Hashemite Arab Federation row (Cliopatria 1415-1439, lower Iraq and Khuzestan) is really the Jalayirid rump and then Qara Qoyunlu land, see that dossier.
Gazetteer: every region name resolves (validated with --resolve); Erciş and Amid are not in places.jsonl and were avoided (capital coordinates are given directly). fx-15 (F157): the Kerman gain moved from 1453 to 1463 and a Tabriz gain was added at Sardrud (April 1408); ledger indices after the 1408 contest_end shifted by one. fx-15 also removed the 1409 Sultaniyya gain and Zanjan from the 1410-1446 keyframes; the review reverted that, because the Qara Qoyunlu page dates the Timurid capture of Sultaniya and Qazvin to 1447.
